_note: The seven English sentences every IndicF5 run in this project has used, frozen. They were previously derived at call time as sentences(scripted_text['en'])[:7], where sentences() drops anything under 25 characters — so 'Simple, right?', "It isn't.", 'So what do we do?' and 'Nine needed stretching.' were silently excluded, and three call sites (indicf5_english.py, four_arm.py, english_check.py) passed different limit/minimum defaults. Which sentences 'fixture7' means is now a recorded decision rather than a regex side effect. The excluded list is kept because the short ones are the bucket real dubbing segments live in: adding them is a deliberate change to make, not a filter to forget. Source: fixtures/scripted_text.json, which is what was read aloud in fixtures/english_speech.wav.

sentences.text: Let me tell you what this project actually does.
You give it a video — a lecture, an interview, anything with clear speech — and it gives you back the same video speaking Hindi.
Hindi takes about twenty percent longer to say than the English it replaces, and the words still have to land in the same three seconds.
We generate six different translations for every sentence, measure how long each one would take to speak, and keep the one that fits without losing the meaning.
Last week the system processed forty-seven segments.
Seven were impossible, and we had to rewrite them.

excluded.text: That's the real work — not the models, the arithmetic between them.
